notes: The grid covers the served map (flat3_straight: 239x215 cells at 5 cm from -18.53, -4.38) with half a metre of margin and 1.7 m of height from 15 cm below the floor. A frame integrates voxels within range_max of the camera; an observation from weight_ref_m weighs 1, nearer ones up to weight_cap, farther ones less. band_half_z_m is half the height band around the lidar's plane whose points are exact by construction and may seat a frame on the model; depth_fusion's live flag band_half_z starts from it. The plane itself is never written in a file twice: the node reads it from the published base_link -> laser edge (config/lidar.json's mount is the fallback). camera_band_m is the height band the camera speaks for (the band /depth_scan marks in, pepin.depth): the slice the camera sources localise against and the one that carries seats and tabletops, pepin.worldmap. window_recentre_m is how far the cart may travel from the window's centre before a volume painted in the ODOMETRY frame (depth_fusion's volume_frame odom, which is the default) slides its box onto the cart and forgets what leaves it: local obstacle memory follows the cart, pepin.tsdf.WindowShift. 2.0 m is chosen against what the window must still hold at the moment it is furthest off centre: the marks' fan reaches 3.0 m (pepin.volume_scan.MARKS_RANGE_M) and the camera integrates to range_max_m, so on this grid's shorter side (250 voxels, a half-extent of 6.25 m) the cart keeps at least 4.25 m of painted memory in every direction, and at a drive's 0.2 m/s one slide is paid about every ten seconds. It is not read at all under volume_frame map, where the volume is the room and stands still. max_weight 20.0 is how fast the volume forgets: a voxel's weight saturates there, so one free observation of weight w moves its field 1/(20+w) of the way to empty and a surface that is gone needs log(1-0.25)/log(20/(20+w)) of them to stop reading occupied. At 60.0, where this stood until 2026-09-22, the camera's background at 2 m (w 1.0 at 6 fps) took 2.9 s to clear and at 1 m 0.75 s; at 20.0 the same two are 1.0 s and 0.27 s, and a depthless ray's own carve (pepin.tsdf.DepthLaw, w 0.34) clears a saturated phantom in 17 frames by this law and 18 measured on the taped frames of 2026-09-22, 2.8 s (scratch/one_localiser/volume_ab.py), where at 60.0 the same obstacle never cleared at all. It is also the lidar's own cap already (pepin.worldmap.LidarLaw.max_weight 20.0), so the two sensors now saturate at the same confidence instead of the camera's outweighing the beams three to one.
